creem.activation_decision_2026-09-05: NOT activating now, despite approval. Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/checkout infrastructure -- the same job Stripe already does live for this experiment (prod_V8TDzCnDU7y2r9, $19, Managed Payments + automatic tax). Approval removes the 'is it usable' uncertainty but does not create a Net-Profit case on its own: no buyer would newly discover the product through Creem (it has no marketplace/search surface, unlike Etsy or Gumroad), so building it would only offer existing buyers a second checkout for the same product -- pure substitution, not incremental reach. Building it now would cost real AI-compute (product config, checkout integration, workflow, docs, cost-ledger wiring) for zero expected incremental revenue, while Etsy (validated buyer search-intent, going live this same iteration) and watching Gumroad/Etsy for a first sale are both higher-expected-value uses of the same budget. Would reconsider only if a specific advantage over Stripe surfaces (e.g. materially lower fees, a market/currency Stripe can't serve, or a partner/embed distribution channel unique to Creem) -- none identified as of this decision.
creem.assessment: Even with account + API + approval all confirmed, Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/billing infrastructure -- functionally the same job Stripe already does live, not a marketplace with its own buyer-search discovery. No distribution-value differentiator over Stripe has been identified. Deprioritized: approved and usable, but NOT being activated absent a specific identified advantage (would be redundant payment infra).

Detected on the next sync, root-caused, and cleaned up: restored status/etsy_listing.json to the canonical listing (4569271638) and deactivated the duplicate via the new scripts/etsy_deactivate_listing.mjs (confirmed INACTIVE via a live API call). Full incident record: status/EVENTS.jsonl (duplicate_listing_incident). Attribution correction, same day: that record only said the triggering run was 'not this session' -- a separate, concurrent Claude session cross-referenced its own actions_run_trigger call (created_at 2026-09-05T01:01:46Z, exact match) and identified the duplicate-causing trigger as its own idempotency-verification re-run, not an anonymous third party. Recorded in status/EVENTS.jsonl (attribution_correction) for an accurate account. All three digital-product channels (Stripe, Gumroad, Etsy) are live for the first time in this experiment's history; revenue remains ¥0 -- reported honestly as 'three channels live', explicitly distinct from 'a sale has occurred.' SAME DAY, LATER (owner-approved priority list executed, then the actual 20:07 JST scheduled cadence run at 20:10 JST): Gumroad's 'Other' category was fixed to 'self-improvement/productivity' (taxonomy_id 85, live-verified); the Etsy re-diagnostic was deliberately deferred (listing too young, gated to ~2026-09-06T00:55Z); Gumroad's view-count blind spot was confirmed genuinely AI-unreachable (session-cookie-gated dashboard controller) and exactly one low-priority human ask was queued. The 20:10 JST scheduled run then re-observed reality with fresh evidence rather than assuming carry-over: live Stripe MCP query confirmed 0 charges and 0 checkout sessions; the latest sales-monitor Action run (04:30 UTC) confirmed 0 new Gumroad sales; no open GitHub issues exist (no 'Promotion blocked'); the Etsy diagnostic timing gate has not yet been reached. No new capability was granted, no market signal changed, and no economically rational action was available beyond what the owner-directed session already executed earlier today -- per the loop's own cost-control rule (section 13), this run recorded the observation and stopped early rather than manufacture busywork. Cadence held at 1x/day; next scheduled fire (2026-09-06 20:07 JST) naturally falls after the Etsy re-diagnostic gate. Day 6 (2026-09-06, actual 20:07 JST run): the Etsy re-diagnostic gate passed and was executed (views 0->2, num_favorers still 0) and, independently, a live Stripe MCP query found the first-ever real checkout-session activity on the Stripe store (2 sessions, both created today, still open/unpaid, $19 each) after 13 days of flat zero. No completed sale on any channel. Audited store/index.html's buy-button wiring for a possible checkout-abandonment defect and found none. n=2 on two channels is real but statistically too small to differentiate channels or justify any price/product/lane change -- held steady, no new channel, no pricing change, no resource reallocation. Cadence held at 1x/day (still economically rational: the free Actions layer covers routine sales detection between daily runs, and this run's own cost was modest). Flagged, but did not build, a real observability gap: no web analytics exist on index.html/store/, so the source of the 2 new Stripe visits is unrecoverable -- worth revisiting only if repeat real traffic appears.
